title: System Location Discovery: System Language Discovery
shortTitle: System Location Discovery: System Language Discovery
summary: This sub technique narrows location discovery to the language and locale settings of a host. Malware and operators read those values to decide whether a machine is worth infecting, often to avoid systems in countries where law enforcement attention or prosecution is more likely. On Windows the checks appear as registry queries against the national language support keys and as calls to API functions that return user and system language identifiers or the keyboard layout list. On macOS and Linux the same information comes from the locale command and the language environment variable, which are trivial to read and leave little trace beyond process execution. The behaviour is not malicious on its own, because installers, agents, and management software read locale constantly. Separating it from that noise needs context: the parent process, whether the read is part of a burst of environment checks, and whether the same program then exits quietly or continues.

beginner.definition: This is one small part of system location discovery, which is the wider search for clues about where a computer is. The parent technique gathers many clues, such as time zone and address. This sub technique looks only at the language and region settings of the machine. An attacker uses the answer to guess which country it is in.
beginner.whyItMatters: This check is cheap, quiet, and often runs before anything harmful happens. It can decide whether your machine is attacked or quietly left alone. Because the same read is normal in many programs, it is easy to dismiss. Knowing the real sources of language data helps you spot the odd cases.
howItWorks: The program starts and reads the language settings before it does anything else.
On Windows it may read a registry key that holds national language information.
It may instead call a system function that returns the language identifier.
On Linux or macOS it reads the locale command output or the language variable.
If the language is on the avoid list, the program may stop and do nothing.
If it is not, the program continues and carries out its real purpose.
beginner.example: Imagine a door to door salesman who only knocks on houses where a certain newspaper is delivered. He walks the street reading doormats, nameplates, and letterboxes before deciding where to knock. Most residents never see him at all, because he passes their door without a sound. He is not checking whether anyone is home. He is checking whether this is the kind of household he wants to visit.
takeaways: Language settings are used as a quick test of which country a machine is in.
The same read is normal, so you must judge it by context and timing.
A program that exits early after a language check is worth investigating.

objectives: Explain how this sub technique differs from the parent location discovery technique.
Name the Windows data sources that hold system language information.
Describe the Linux and macOS equivalents of a system language check.
Explain why language checks are used to avoid certain countries.
Identify contextual clues that separate malicious language checks from normal ones.
